question: Should OpenClaw core support native cross-gateway session messaging now, and if so should it use a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool path or wait for the broader gateway federation contract?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses gateway, session-state, message-delivery, and credential trust boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or security model.

options.title: Design the federation contract first
options.body: Use #43605 as the concrete session-messaging tracker while aligning it with gateway federation, mutual auth, scopes, replay handling, and transcript ownership before merging code.

options.title: Advance the linked narrow PR
options.body: Allow PR #43656 to proceed only after conflicts, security review, upgrade behavior, and real multi-gateway proof are resolved.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Close or downgrade the core request only if maintainers explicitly choose documented plugin/MCP/channel workarounds instead of native cross-gateway session routing.

recommendation.title: Design the federation contract first
recommendation.body: Use #43605 as the concrete session-messaging tracker while aligning it with gateway federation, mutual auth, scopes, replay handling, and transcript ownership before merging code.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for session-tool routing and security scoping is in this person's prior merged work.
